steps.assert: This is the immediately-pre-write assertion against CURRENT main, not the historical bootstrap head that sequence 2 read. Set current_main_sha to the endpoint response's full sha. In the apply operator's local clone, run local_git.prepare in order: if the clone is shallow, unshallow it read-only from the explicit jerudnik/jcode URL, then fetch both exact commits. Run every local_git assertion. The final path-limited git diff compares endpoint tree/blob identity for every protected path without an API file-count cap or silent truncation. It also handles renames explicitly: moving a protected path outside the protected prefixes is a deletion of the old protected path and fails; moving a path into a protected prefix is an addition and fails; moving within the protected set also fails. A zero diff, including current_main_sha == bootstrap_merge_sha, passes. Together with sequence 2's context-emission proof, this proves the reviewed protected bytes are exactly what current main contains immediately before sequence 7 requires the contexts.
steps.on_mismatch: stop before any write. If unshallow/fetch fails, either commit is unavailable, the clone remains shallow, or bootstrap_merge_sha is not an ancestor of current_main_sha, treat this as an unverifiable or rewritten main boundary and a governance incident. If git diff is non-zero, a protected path was added, deleted, renamed, or content-modified after the bootstrap merge; re-review current main's actual workflow/manifest state, capture a fresh bootstrap_merge_sha-equivalent baseline if appropriate, and re-run from sequence 1. Do not require a context whose current-main definition was not just proved identical to what was reviewed.

abort_policy: Stop before the next write whenever a read_assert or checkpoint fails. No write may run before sequences 1-6 have all passed. Never continue to sequence 15 unless sequence 14 passed.
residual_risk: Every rule written here can be rewritten or deleted by the repository owner-admin, who is the accepted root of trust for this personal repository per DECISIONS.md D031. This apply document does not claim to prevent that; it makes the intended state explicit and machine-comparable, proves current main's protected-path bytes match what was reviewed immediately before the first write (sequence 6), and repeats that proof immediately after sequence 8 while rollback remains available. GitHub's ruleset PUT has no expected-main-SHA precondition, so a residual race remains after that repeat and before the apply completes; the repeat narrows but cannot eliminate it. A protected-path merge observed by the repeat triggers rollback, and later drift is detected by scripts/fork-health.sh --live and the governance fixtures.
